message.content:
**Paris Getaway – 7‑Day Itinerary (Mid‑Season, €1,200–€1,800 per person)** | Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | |-----|---------|-----------|---------| | **Day 1 – Arrival & Orientation** | • Arrive at Charles de Gaulle or Orly.
• Take the RER B to your hotel in the 7th or 8th arrondissement (close to the Eiffel Tower and Louvre).
• Check‑in, freshen up. | • Light stroll along the Seine, cross the Pont Alexandre III.
• Visit the **Eiffel Tower** (book tickets online to skip the line). | • Dinner at **Le Jules Verne** (reservation recommended) or a cozy bistro in the Latin Quarter.
• Optional night cruise on the Seine (Bateaux Mouches). | | **Day 2 – Classic Louvre & Palais Royal** | • Early breakfast at **Café Marly**.
• Louvre Museum (focus on the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and the Egyptian Antiquities).
• Take a guided audio tour for deeper context. | • Walk to the **Palais Royal** gardens, explore the boutiques.
• Lunch at **Café de la Paix** (classic French cuisine). | • Attend a performance at the **Opéra Garnier** (check schedule).
• Late‑night walk to the **Arc de Triomphe** for city lights. | | **Day 3 – Montmartre & Sacré‑Coeur** | • Breakfast at **Le Pain Quotidien**.
• Explore Montmartre: Sacré‑Coeur, Place du Tertre, and the artists’ square.
• Visit the **Musée de Montmartre**. | • Lunch at **La Maison Rose**.
• Take the funicular or walk down to the **Eiffel Tower** area for a panoramic view. | • Dinner at **Le Coq Rico** (roast chicken).
• Optional jazz club in the Latin Quarter (e.g., **Le Caveau de la Huchette**). | | **Day 4 – Day Trip to Versailles** | • Early train to Versailles (RER C).
• Tour the **Palace of Versailles** (Hall of Mirrors, Royal Apartments). | • Picnic in the **Gardens of Versailles** (pre‑order a picnic basket).
• Explore the **Trianon Palaces** and **Marie Antoinette’s Estate**. | • Return to Paris.
• Light dinner near your hotel or a quick bite at **L’As du Fallafel** on Rue des Rosiers. | | **Day 5 – Modern Art & Canal Saint‑Martin** | • Breakfast at **Café Kitsuné**.
• Visit the **Centre Pompidou** (modern art, design).
• Explore the **Le Marais** district (boutiques, art galleries). | • Lunch at **L’As du Fallafel** or **Café Charlot**.
• Walk along the **Canal Saint‑Martin**, stop at a café for a coffee. | • Dinner at **Septime** (reservations required).
• Night walk along the **Pont Neuf** and the **Île de la Cité**. | | **Day 6 – Shopping & Relaxation** | • Breakfast at **Du Pain et des Idées**.
• Shopping on the **Champs‑Élysées** and **Rue du Faubourg Saint‑Haussmann**.
• Visit the **Galeries Lafayette** for a panoramic view from the roof. | • Lunch at **Le Grand Café**.
• Relax at the **Jardin du Luxembourg** (boat rental, book a table at the café). | • Farewell dinner at **Le Cinq** (Michelin‑starred) or a classic brasserie like **Bistro Paul Bert**. | | **Day 7 – Departure** | • Pack, check‑out.
• Quick visit to **Notre‑Dame** (outside, as interior may still be under restoration). | • Grab a croissant and coffee at **Café de Flore**.
• Last stroll along the Seine. | • Head to the airport via RER or taxi. | ### Practical Tips | Topic | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Transportation** | Buy a **Paris Visite** pass (valid for 2–5 days) covering metro, buses, and RER within zones 1–3. | | **Accommodation** | Stay in the 7th, 8th, or 4th arrondissements for centrality. Look for boutique hotels or Airbnb with a view of the Seine. | | **Dining** | Book restaurants 2–3 weeks in advance, especially for Michelin‑starred places. | | **Tickets** | Pre‑book major attractions (Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Versailles, Centre Pompidou) online to avoid queues. | | **Language** | Basic French phrases help; most staff speak English. | | **Weather** | Mid‑season (May–June) is mild (15–22 °C). Pack layers and an umbrella. | | **Safety** | Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas; use a money belt. | --- Would you like to use the function to sort an array of numbers?
